status_summary: EO 14210 (2025-02-11) ordered agency RIF plans and a limit of one hire per four departures; the Supreme Court stayed an injunction against it on 2025-07-08 without ruling on specific RIF plans. Section 120 of the stopgap funding law approved 2025-11-12 (Public Law 119-37) barred federal funds for starting, noticing or carrying out RIFs through 2026-01-30 and voided RIFs taken from 2025-10-01 to enactment, and OPM's memo of 2025-11-13 told agencies to rescind such notices; on 2025-12-17 a federal judge in the Northern District of California issued a preliminary injunction in AFGE v. OMB that bars RIF implementation through 2026-01-30 and requires rescission of certain RIFs (about 680 employees at Education, State, SBA and GSA, per Maryland Matters), and the government filed a notice of appeal on 2025-12-22. That bar has expired. EO 14356 (2025-10-15) set a continuing rule, after the January 2025 freeze, requiring approval of each vacancy by an agency strategic hiring committee, and OPM issued annual staffing plan guidance on 2026-07-30. OPM's final RIF rule (91 FR 49178, published 2026-08-03, effective 2026-09-02) restructures tenure groups and, within each retention register, ranks employees by performance credit plus veterans' preference points, with tenure subgroup and then length of service used only to break ties; per OPM's memo, appeals of new RIF actions go to OPM instead of the MSPB. OPM's data site showed 2,020,230 civilian employees in July 2026; OPM said departures in the year would reach about 317,000, mostly voluntary, including about 154,000 through the Deferred Resignation Program, a buyout-style approach the Mandate cautions can raise costs. A litigation tracker updated 2026-10-05 reports no injunction against the OPM rules that took effect 2026-09-02; a four-union suit filed 2026-08-25 challenges the suitability and performance rules. A fiscal 2027 continuing resolution (H.R. 6500, reported signed by Fox News in September 2026) funds the government through 2026-12-11 (Sec. 106(3)); a search of the enrolled bill text found no reduction-in-force provision.

timeline.event: EO 14210 directs OMB to plan workforce reduction, sets a limit of one hire per four departures with exceptions, requires large-scale RIF preparations (excluding public safety, immigration enforcement and law enforcement), and creates agency DOGE Team Leads for hiring review.

In Trump v. AFGE (No. 24A1174), the Supreme Court grants a stay of a N.D. Cal. injunction against EO 14210 and the related OMB/OPM memo, saying the government is likely to succeed on lawfulness and expressing no view on any agency RIF plan. Justice Sotomayor concurred and Justice Jackson dissented.
timeline.source: Supreme Court of the United States

timeline.event: EO 14356 sets a continuing rule that no vacant civilian position is filled or created except as provided, requires strategic hiring committees within 30 days and annual staffing plans, with exclusions for national security, public safety and some noncareer posts.

The stopgap funding law Public Law 119-37 (H.R. 5371) is approved. Its section 120 bars federal funds for initiating, noticing or carrying out a reduction in force through 2026-01-30 (with exceptions for voluntary separations, court-ordered actions and orderly shutdown) and gives no force or effect to RIFs taken between 2025-10-01 and enactment, with notices rescinded and employees restored with back pay. OPM's memo of 2025-11-13 implements it.

OPM Associate Director Veronica Hinton issues a memo to chief human capital officers on RIF actions affected by the Continuing Appropriations Act, 2026: RIF notices issued from 2025-10-01 to 2025-11-12 are rescinded within 5 days with restoration and back pay, and no RIF may be initiated or noticed through 2026-01-30; non-RIF performance and conduct actions and probationary terminations may proceed.

Judge Susan Illston (N.D. Cal., AFGE v. OMB, No. 3:25-cv-08302) grants a preliminary injunction that bars implementation of RIFs through 2026-01-30 and requires rescission of certain RIFs; Maryland Matters (reporting Federal News Network) describes the order as covering shutdown-period RIFs at Education, State, SBA and GSA for about 680 employees. The government files a notice of appeal on 2025-12-22 (Ninth Circuit No. 25-7998).

OPM states that about 317,000 federal employees would leave in 2025, over 90 percent through voluntary programs and attrition, including about 154,000 Deferred Resignation Program resignations, and about 68,000 hires (OPM's own claims; date from OPM news listing).
OPM's workforce data site shows 2,020,230 federal civilian employees (data as of July 2026; day set to the first of the month; some Department of War components had not submitted June and July data).

OPM issues FY2027 annual staffing plan guidance implementing EO 14356, with plans due 2026-09-30 and governmentwide hiring targets (for example 60 percent of external competitive selections from shared certificates).

OPM final rule on Reduction in Force published (91 FR 49178): performance credit and veterans' preference points set retention standing, tenure groups simplified, probationary and some temporary employees excluded from competition.
The RIF rule takes effect for notices issued on or after this date; OPM memo describes 60-day notice (not less than 30 with approval) and appeals to OPM rather than the MSPB.

Fox News reports that the President signed H.R. 6500, the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (the date shown is the article date, not a stated signing date). The enrolled bill text on govinfo.gov, searched for this pass, has no reduction-in-force provision and funds agencies through 2026-12-11 (Sec. 106(3)); Nextgov's coverage of the House vote also names no RIF limit.

A federal-workforce litigation tracker updated this date reports no injunction against OPM's RIF-appeals and other personnel rules that took effect 2026-09-02; a four-union suit filed 2026-08-25 challenges the suitability and performance rules, not the RIF rule.

title: Control workforce size through hiring limits and RIFs ranked by performance first
uncertainties: Workforce totals (2,020,230; 317,000 departures; 154,000 deferred resignations; 68,000 hires) are OPM's own figures with no independent baseline checked. The Mandate cautions against buyouts, while the administration used a Deferred Resignation Program; this is a difference in approach, not a judgment on costs. The January 2025 hiring freeze memorandum was not fetched. The November 2025 RIF bar was read in Public Law 119-37 (section 120) and in OPM's implementing memo; the December 2025 N.D. Cal. injunction was read through the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse summary and Maryland Matters, not the order itself, and the ruling's later course in the Ninth Circuit (No. 25-7998) was not checked. A proposed settlement in AFGE v. OMB reported in September 2026 concerns the rescinded shutdown RIF memo and contingency plans and does not reach the OPM RIF rule. The OPM final RIF rule was re-read in the Federal Register (91 FR 49178, effective 2026-09-02; corrected 2026-08-25 at 91 FR 54794 per OPM's memo) and its appeal forum in OPM's memo of 2026-09-02, but the Federal Register text past the first 100,000 characters (including the appeals discussion) was not read. Litigation status as of 2026-10-05 comes from a secondary tracker. The H.R. 6500 enrolled text carries no enactment date, so the signing date rests on Fox News; the absence of a RIF provision rests on the fetch tool's search of the enrolled text.
